title: NAF: Zero-Shot Feature Upsampling via Neighborhood Attention Filtering
mechanism: Encoder-agnostic zero-shot upsampler: cross-scale neighbourhood attention with RoPE guided only by the high-res image, a learned joint bilateral filter that lifts any VFM's patch features to pixel resolution.
adaptation: Lift frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 (or 7B) 32x32 tokens to 512x512 using the 1-channel EL cell replicated to 3 channels as guidance; light conv head over 24 classes. Check that sub-2%-contrast cracks are not smoothed by the bilateral weighting along finger and busbar edges.
min_experiment: Frozen DINOv3 ViT-S and ViT-L 1x1 probe: NAF at 512 vs bilinear at 512 vs bilinear at 1024 input (existing 0.212 crack AP for ViT-S). Metric F51 + 5-fold CV crack AP and gridline AP. Kill: NAF at 512 does not beat bilinear at 1024 on crack AP. About 3 GPU-h.
prior_overlap: Partial: frozen linear probes of DINOv3 / DINOv2 / SAM2 used bilinear upsampling only. No learned upsampler was tested, so open.
evidence: R: Pascal VOC probe with DINOv3-B 87.85 mIoU vs JAFAR 87.10; runs on DINOv3-7B where VFM-specific upsamplers run out of memory; 2K feature maps at 18 FPS. Object-scale benchmarks only.
